observations.explanation: The benchmark is described as combining interaction with simulated users, API tools, and domain-specific policies, and its reward compares the final database state and user-facing responses with annotated outcomes. The paper also says dialogue wording may vary while reaching the same database outcome (PDF pp. 1–4).
The paper defines pass^k over repeated trials and reports that the best-performing gpt-4o function-calling agent has pass^8 below 25% in τ-retail (PDF pp. 4–5, 7).

The authors explicitly state that reward r = 1 may be necessary but not sufficient for success, giving failure to obtain explicit user confirmation as an example of a policy violation the reward may not capture (PDF p. 4).

The evaluation covers τ-retail and τ-airline; the authors describe medical, tax, and legal domains as possible future work. Thus, transfer to those broader settings is not evaluated in this paper (PDF pp. 2, 5–6).
